title: DataFlex-RL: An Evaluation Platform for RLVR Data Policies

key_results: Uniform GRPO improves accuracy by 7.76pp over baseline; no rollout-selection or reweighting method achieves statistically significant improvement over uniform sampling
comments: Rigorous controlled evaluation across multiple seeds and models reveals the difficulty of improving over simple uniform data policies, with concerning evaluation sensitivity across benchmark subsets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rollout-selection or reweighting methods improve over uniform sampling
hypotheses.result: False - no method achieved 95% CI excluding zero relative improvement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive mixtures outperform fixed equal mixture
hypotheses.result: False - fixed equal mixture remains competitive

title: Feyospace-v1: How the Cyber Mercury Seven Trained Frontier Cyber Models
task: Training open-weight cyber security agents
key_results: Feyospace-s1 achieves 63.24% verified success on CyberGym, ranks 10th on leaderboard; three checkpoints improve by avg 23.76% on full suite, 1st among comparable parameter scales
comments: Demonstrates that data-centric post-training with execution verification and multi-turn supervision can scale cyber agent capability without massive model size, though relies on custom infrastructure.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-turn supervision with execution verification enables comparable-scale models to reach leading cyber capability

title: Benchmark Radar: A Living Database and Search Engine for AI Benchmarks and Evaluation
task: Discovering and cataloging AI benchmarks at scale
key_results: Catalog contains 1,283 source records from 4 benchmarks and 12,916 numeric observations on 790 records; 37 discovery sources with daily updates
comments: A valuable infrastructure contribution for benchmark research, though maintaining ground truth at scale and handling score comparability remain open challenges.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Daily discovery from 37 sources can maintain a comprehensive, up-to-date benchmark catalog

title: Breaking the Vision-Action Shortcut: Latent Interface Training for Generalizable Robotics Foundation Models
task: Improving robot foundation models under visual distribution shifts

comments: Addresses a critical limitation of vision-language-action models by decoupling goal-directed action priors from visual inputs, though evaluation remains largely in simulation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Constraining visual conditioning through pose-supervised latent interface preserves task-relevant spatial info while reducing vision-action shortcuts
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: consistent improvements across four architectures and real-world scenarios

title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking
task: Efficient attention sparsification via end-to-end optimization
key_results: SAS consistently outperforms sparse attention baselines across reasoning, long-context, and agentic tasks; especially large gains under tight attention budgets
comments: Simple yet effective approach that aligns selector optimization directly with downstream loss rather than distilling dense attention, though specific numerical improvements are not quantified.

model_io.model: Transformer with gated sparse attention (SAS mechanism)

hypotheses.hypothesis: End-to-end optimization of context ranking with language modeling loss improves sparse attention over distillation-based methods

task: Efficient skill optimization for LLM agents via contextual bandits
key_results: COBRA-Skills achieves strongest average performance across six benchmarks, reduces optimization cost by 55-58% relative to SkillOpt, uses only 50 examples per benchmark
comments: Combines bandit-based prioritization with evolutionary skill refinement to enable practical skill optimization with limited budget, though evaluation focuses on efficiency rather than absolute skill quality.

model_io.model: LLM agent with skill library (three target models tested)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Contextual-bandit-guided prioritization reduces evaluation cost while maintaining skill optimization performance

title: Bridging historical antigenic profiling and whole-genome taxonomy in Rickettsia
task: Reconcile historical antigenic profiling with whole-genome taxonomy in Rickettsia
key_results: No quantitative metrics provided; review demonstrates structured antigenic relationships align with genetic relatedness within spotted fever, transitional, and typhus groups
comments: This perspective piece effectively bridges serological and genomic approaches but is qualitative; a formal quantitative concordance analysis would strengthen claims about polyphasic taxonomy.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Serological cross-reactivity patterns correlate with genetic relatedness in Rickettsia
hypotheses.result: Supported by literature review; close concordance observed within species groups

title: Frequency-oriented adaptive real-time object detector for cluttered traffic scenes
task: Frequency-domain adaptive object detection for cluttered traffic scenes
key_results: mAP: 90.9% (KITTI), 53.7% (BDD100K), 50.2% (Cityscapes), 53.1% (Waymo) with only 8.77M parameters
comments: Lightweight architecture achieves competitive performance across diverse benchmarks; ablation studies isolating frequency decomposition and fusion contributions not detailed.

model_io.model: Frequency-Oriented Adaptive Detector (Frequency Dynamic Convolution + Adaptive Frequency-Oriented Fusion)
inputs: traffic scene images from KITTI, BDD100K, Cityscapes, Waymo datasets

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frequency Dynamic Convolution with adaptive kernel decomposition balances texture and semantic representations
hypotheses.result: mAP 90.9% (KITTI), 53.7% (BDD100K), 50.2% (Cityscapes), 53.1% (Waymo) achieved

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive Frequency-Oriented Fusion reduces multi-scale feature inconsistencies better than standard fusion
hypotheses.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art detectors with only 8.77M parameters

title: Large language model-enabled automated data extraction for concrete materials informatics
task: Automated extraction and structuring of concrete materials data from scientific literature using LLMs
key_results: F1 score up to 0.98 across diverse LLMs; 9,000 high-quality records extracted in one hour from 27,000 publications; largest open blended cement concrete database created
comments: Pipeline robustness demonstrated across LLM families, but domain-specific accuracy and cost-per-record metrics for scaling to other materials domains not provided.

inputs: unstructured scientific literature abstracts and full texts

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs can reliably extract and structure materials data from unstructured text with high precision
hypotheses.result: F1=0.98 achieved; generalizable across LLM families

hypotheses.hypothesis: Large, diverse, information-rich datasets enhance both in-distribution and out-of-distribution ML generalization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via subsequent ML analyses on constructed database

title: Criteria for unbiased estimation: applications to noise-agnostic sensing and quantum channel estimation
task: Establish necessary and sufficient conditions for local unbiased estimation in multi-parameter quantum tasks
key_results: Derived conditions for quantum state and channel parameter estimation; demonstrated feasibility of unbiased phase estimation under unknown Pauli noise with entangled probe and ancilla
comments: Theoretical framework is elegant but application to realistic many-parameter regimes with practical resource constraints remains open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local unbiased estimation requires specific derivative structure in encoded quantum states
hypotheses.result: Necessary and sufficient conditions derived and validated

hypotheses.hypothesis: Entangled probes with noiseless ancillae enable local unbiased estimation under unknown Pauli noise
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for phase estimation; infeasible with naive scheme

title: Towards autonomous urban drainage modelling: evaluating AI agent architectures for automated SWMM calibration
task: Evaluate AI agent architectures for automated urban drainage model (SWMM) calibration
key_results: Three agent organizations (skill-based, tool-based, multi-agent) all completed calibration successfully; tool-based cheapest but least reliable for extended tasks; multi-agent cost varies with LLM capability
comments: Controlled case study on single SWMM model; real-world heterogeneity and failure modes under production drainage systems not tested.

model_io.model: Skill-based AI agent (instructions consulted on demand)
Tool-based AI agent (fixed interfaces supplied in advance)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Different agent organizations trade off reliability, cost, and LLM capability requirements
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; skill-based sustains longer sequences but requires higher LLM capability; tool-based cheapest but breaks on extended tasks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-agent organization remains reliable across task extensions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with cost varying by LLM choice

title: Hybrid deep learning for smart grid SCADA intrusion detection with mutual information feature selection for smart meter data analysis
task: Hybrid CNN-Transformer-BiGRU architecture for smart grid SCADA intrusion detection
key_results: 88% accuracy, macro F1 0.86, MCC 0.74, ROC-AUC 0.94, 9% false negative rate, 7% false alarm rate, <100 ms latency on commodity hardware
comments: Statistically significant improvement over CNN-only, CNN-LSTM, CNN-Transformer baselines (p<0.001); field validation on live heterogeneous SCADA traffic explicitly noted as future work.

inputs: smart meter telemetry (14,415 held-out samples from MSU benchmark)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Three complementary inductive biases (CNN, Transformer, BiGRU) address temporal motifs, global context, and attack propagation patterns better than two-component hybrids
hypotheses.result: F1 0.86 outperforms CNN-only, CNN-LSTM, CNN-Transformer baselines (p<0.001)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mutual information selection, ADASYN oversampling, and F1-optimized thresholding together eliminate class imbalance and leakage
hypotheses.result: Ablation isolates contribution of each preprocessing stage; 5-fold CV F1=0.87±0.01 confirms stability

title: Uncertainty-aware Bayesian federated learning for low-resource neural machine translation at the edge
task: Federated neural machine translation for low-resource language pairs with uncertainty quantification
key_results: MT-BayesFL achieves BLEU 32.6 (English-Russian) and 28.3 (English-Swahili); 92.1% performance retention at 30% device dropout; 1.786 MB upload per round; epsilon=12.53 privacy
comments: Not uniformly superior on high-resource pairs; privacy accounting conditional on separate aggregate release, and end-to-end privacy-utility claims not made.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Matrix-normal posteriors and covariance-aware aggregation improve low-resource translation and uncertainty quantification
hypotheses.result: BLEU 32.6 (English-Russian) and 28.3 (English-Swahili) with ECE 0.082; outperforms baselines on low-resource pairs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Top-K transmission and KL regularization enable communication-efficient federated training under non-IID data
hypotheses.result: 1.786 MB upload per round; 92.1% performance retention at 30% dropout confirmed

title: Coplanar QCA reversible 4 to 2 encoder architectures for ultra-dense nanoscale systems
task: Design compact reversible 4-to-2 encoders in quantum-dot cellular automata
key_results: Priority encoder: 28 cells, 0.06 μm²; hybrid encoder: 19 cells, 0.03 μm²; both 73% cell-count reduction and 62% area reduction versus recent prior work
comments: Deposition-fault analysis confirms robustness, but scalability to larger encoder widths and manufacturing yield implications are not discussed.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Optimized majority-based primitives minimize cell count and area
hypotheses.result: 73% cell reduction and 62% area reduction achieved

hypotheses.hypothesis: Two-clock-zone computation is sufficient for reversible 4-to-2 encoding
hypotheses.result: Both designs complete within two clock zones confirmed

title: Contract and digital chains: the effect of dual-chain coupling on farmers’ credit access
task: Assess dual-chain coupling effect on farmers' credit access under information asymmetry
key_results: Dual-chain coupling significantly increases credit amount and likelihood of obtaining credit; contract and digital chains independently positive; effect stronger for educated farmers and weaker in grain-producing regions
comments: Nonlinear analysis reveals threshold effect requiring moderate-to-high coordination; cross-sectional design limits causal inference despite mechanistic channels identified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual-chain coupling reduces information asymmetry and improves repayment capacity assessment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via income and information efficiency channel analyses

hypotheses.hypothesis: Coordination threshold exists below which joint benefits are undetectable
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nonlinear effect emerges only at moderate-to-high chain coordination levels

title: Multi-Agent collaboration as a complementary architecture for AI-generated medical examination items
task: Multi-agent LLM collaboration for generating medical examination items
key_results: Multi-agent outputs received 57.7% expert preference vs. 42.3% for single-model baseline in blinded evaluation on China's National Medical Licensing Examination
comments: Small sample size and single evaluation domain (Chinese medical licensing); generalization to other high-stakes assessments and languages unclear.

model_io.model: Multi-agent LLM system (drafting, critique, adversarial refinement agents)
outputs: medical examination items with higher-order reasoning quality

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-agent decomposition (drafting, critique, adversarial refinement) overcomes single-LLM limits in higher-order reasoning
hypotheses.result: 57.7% expert preference for multi-agent vs. 42.3% for single-model baseline confirmed

title: Metamaterial-enabled battery-free wireless sensor networks for unencumbered human-machine interactions
task: Enable battery-free wireless sensor networks via dual-mode metamaterial textiles
key_results: 37.8× data throughput enhancement; 2× wireless power transfer efficiency vs. near-field clothing; robust multimodal HMI sensing during motion
comments: Practical demonstration of ultra-wideband metamaterial integration, though long-term textile durability under repeated deformation untested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual-mode metamaterial simultaneously supports efficient power transfer and Bluetooth communication
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via wearable robotic control, VR, and digital twin demonstrations

title: Efficient power generation near room temperature in earth-abundant thermoelectric tin sulfide via lattice ordering
task: Enhance room-temperature thermoelectric performance of tin sulfide via lattice ordering
key_results: zT ~1.06 at 300 K, ~2.0 at 573 K in Ag-doped SnS; power factor ~101 μW cm⁻¹K⁻²; conversion efficiency ~3.3%, output power density ~0.31 W cm⁻²
comments: Significant improvement for earth-abundant material through multiband engineering; practical module scaling remains to be demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ag substitution enhances lattice dynamical anisotropy and enables multiband valence structure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via high mobility, metallic conductivity, and elevated zT

title: Observation of stick-slip behavior with structural superlubric characteristics
task: Characterize stick-slip behavior with superlubric properties
key_results: Coefficient of friction near zero with wear-free long-distance sliding in Au/graphite system below critical velocity; static-dynamic friction asymmetry driven by point defect pinning
comments: Intriguing coexistence of opposing phenomena, though velocity dependence suggests regime-specific applicability to practical devices.

model_io.model: Au mesa on graphite substrate tribological system

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stick-slip emerges from superlubric incommensurate interface with weak point-defect pinning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; bond formation/rupture at vacancy defects drives asymmetry

title: Microwave-to-optical transduction using magnon–exciton coupling
task: Realize coherent microwave-to-optical transduction via magnon-exciton coupling
key_results: Coherent conversion over ~300-MHz intrinsic bandwidth in bulk CrSBr without cavity; higher cooperativity achievable via reduced magnetic volume and cavity integration
comments: Novel use of resonant exciton-magnon coupling circumvents weak off-resonant magneto-optical effects; scalability to quantum networks requires further integration studies.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Magnon modulation of excitonic susceptibility generates broadband coherent optical sidebands
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; multiple exciton-polariton resonances inherit magnon-coupled response

title: Single-gate, multipartite entanglement on a room-temperature quantum register
task: Demonstrate parallel multi-qubit entangling gates at room temperature
key_results: Four-qubit GHZ state generation in 14.8 μs (10× faster than sequential); fidelity 0.92(4) vs. 0.69(3) for sequential approach; parallel 3-qubit gates demonstrated
comments: Remarkable speed-up and fidelity improvement suggests scalable path to entanglement in practical solid-state devices.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parallelized gates exploit hyperfine coupling frequencies to generate multipartite entanglement faster than sequential gates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 4-qubit gate fidelity improved to 0.92 vs. 0.69 sequentially

title: Demonstration of on-chip all-optical switching of magnetization in integrated photonics
task: Demonstrate on-chip all-optical magnetization switching in photonic circuits
key_results: 90% switching contrast in 500-nm devices; 14.8 μs switching time; fidelity ~92% for integrated approach vs. 69% sequential gate performance
comments: Major step toward integrated spintronic-photonic systems, though spatial non-uniformity limits larger devices and stochastic switching.

model_io.model: Silicon nitride photonic circuit with Co/Gd Hall cross
inputs: femtosecond laser pulses through on-chip waveguides

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-uniform optical absorption causes reduced contrast and stochastic switching in larger devices
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via finite-element simulations of domain-wall dynamics

title: Generation of a high-intensity, superthermal muonium beam for gravity and laser spectroscopy experiments
task: Generate high-brightness muonium beam for gravity and spectroscopy tests
key_results: Superthermal beam extraction from superfluid helium with yields matching highest diffuse sources; enables percent-level gravitational acceleration measurement and sub-kHz 1S-2S spectroscopy
comments: Novel approach to overcome short muon lifetime; crucial for testing gravity with second-generation Standard Model particles.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Superfluid helium enables high-brightness muonium beam extraction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; yields comparable to diffuse sources with narrow velocity spread

title: An algorithm to generate two-dimensional critical lattice models using competing anyon condensation
task: Generate 2D critical lattice models via competing anyon condensation
key_results: Systematic generation of infinite family of critical lattice models; recovery of Haagerup symmetries and identification of 3 candidate CFTs; critical couplings encoded in string-net algebraic data
comments: Elegant bridge between topological order and CFT classification, though experimental realization of these lattice models remains unexplored.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-commuting anyon condensation generates critical points
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via systematic model generation

title: Electrification mechanisms in sliding liquid and frozen drops
task: Elucidate microscopic mechanisms of slide electrification in liquid and frozen drops
key_results: Frozen polar liquids retain substantial charge despite reduced ion mobility; non-polar liquids show identical liquid/frozen charging; findings indicate electron transfer mechanism complements ion transfer
comments: Challenges ion-transfer-only paradigm; bidirectional charge mechanism suggests electronegativity and phase-dependent pathways.

model_io.model: Sliding drop tribochemistry on insulating surfaces

hypotheses.hypothesis: At least two charge transfer mechanisms operate: ion transfer (temperature-dependent) and electron transfer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via comparison of liquid and frozen polar/non-polar compounds

title: Comparative study of femtosecond laser ablation of glass using ultrathin gold and nickel films as sensitizers
task: Compare Au and Ni ultrathin-film sensitization of femtosecond laser glass ablation
key_results: Au more effective sensitizer than Ni; hot-electron interfacial coupling dominates over phonon-phonon mechanisms; relative energy-transfer strength determines sensitizer effectiveness
comments: Clarifies metal-sensitized ablation physics via electron-phonon coupling, relevant for precision laser micromachining.

model_io.model: Femtosecond laser ablation with ultrathin metal sensitizers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hot-electron interfacial coupling via metal films mediates dielectric sensitization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; relative interfacial/bulk phonon coupling strength determines effectiveness
